note_on_recording: No held-out dataset of this round (v6 fresh seeds, 523..786) had been recorded, opened or scored when this file was committed (backstage --only commit, then the repo copy); the held-out look-0 recording starts after that commit. Dev = the 24 v6 train/validation seeds (91 known tray objects), recorded fresh for this round and used for no tuning: the heavy reader and the replace rule were chosen on the older dev batch (seeds 235..275, text reads only).
splits: ros_ws/src/restocker_benchmarks/config/perception_splits_v6.json (embedded sha256 2aaee90575d037447fadbdd118aec063b4a385944279ea99fff92c22613e34c1, file sha256 109dcd54f3ed8916bd8d54c08043e9614ac53d38fbbb0e18f57cb32cf228d661); v1-v5 untouched; round 3's decision seeds 365..522 (and 285..364) are burned in it

heavy_reader.rule: only on a look the cheap reader left open; its tokens replace the cheap tokens of that look; margin, contradiction, shortlist and twin rules unchanged

arms.off: barcode decode disabled AND the aimed barcode close-up views are not shown to the ladder (headline: a product without a barcode never gets those views)
arms.off_views: round 3's off arm: decode disabled, every view kept (reported for comparison)

decision_unit: one tray object, looks accumulated up to 3 re-looks; every recorded v6 fresh held-out seed counts; a seed that cannot be recorded after six attempts is reported, never dropped quietly

bound_notes.coverage_floors: Each floor is the dev (24 v6 seeds, 91 known objects, 3 re-looks) lower 95% Wilson limit rounded down to 0.05: off 66/91 = 72.5% [62.6, 80.6] -> 0.60; off_views 71/91 = 78.0% [68.5, 85.3] -> 0.65; on 75/91 = 82.4% [73.3, 88.9] -> 0.70. Round 3's dev (68%) overstated its held-out (49.7%) by about 18 points; these floors are met on held-out only if the lower Wilson limit there reaches them.
bound_notes.relooks_mean_max: 1.2 for the headline arm: with the aimed barcode views removed the off arm names later (dev: 0.94 mean re-looks of named, 0.37 with the views, 0.27 with the barcode). Round 3's 0.5 belonged to an arm that had those views. Judged on the headline arm only.
bound_notes.latency: p95 per look (cheap ladder, headline arm; dev 1.46 s, off_views 2.45 s) keeps round 3's 4000 ms and EXCLUDES the heavy reader; the heavy reader has its own budget, p95 per escalated read (2 crops, Florence-2 base, 4 CPU threads, a loaded 32-core box): dev mean 18.6 s, p95 22.8 s, bound 40 s.
bound_notes.wrong_after_heavy_read: named objects whose decision used the heavy reader and whose name is wrong, over the whole run (round 3's wrong_after_escalation, re-look wrong, stays and is separate)
bound_notes.unknown: dev has no unregistered product; an offline replay of the recorded dev looks with each object's true product removed from the registry named a registered product in 6/91 (off) and 8/91 (off_views) objects, mostly GEN-017 boxes whose twin was removed (a twin whose sibling is unregistered has no tie to refuse on). The held-out unknown set is the two unregistered bottles of the identity round (GEN-008, GEN-011), where round 3 named 0/50; this proxy says the unknown bound may be at risk. Policy not changed (brief: keep the margin rule and twin policy).

required_sample.note: 240 fresh held-out seeds hold about 840 known and 85 unregistered-twin tray objects (round 3: 489 and 50 per 140 seeds). Named objects per arm = coverage x known: 400 is met by every arm if coverage is at least 0.48; below that the false-identity bound is inconclusive on sample size, not passed.

pass_rule: false identity and unknown named: upper Wilson limit under the bound and sample met = pass; point estimate over the bound = fail; else inconclusive. Coverage passes only if the lower Wilson limit reaches its floor (fail if the point estimate is under it). Latency, re-look and wrong-after bounds are plain comparisons on the headline arm (the heavy-read bounds on the arm that ran the heavy reader; not_exercised if nothing was escalated). One run, no re-run after a fail.
